mainTopic: Covering feces and a scorpion on שבת, when harmful creatures may be killed on שבת, and related stories and rulings
overview: This amud opens with a story: רב חנן בר רבא hears רבי אבין teaching that one may cover a child's feces with a bowl on שבת. He objects that such feces are fit for dogs and may simply be moved, so he corrects the text to chicken feces. The גמרא then asks why chicken feces could not be removed as a גרף של רעי. After several back-and-forths it settles on a garbage heap inside a courtyard. Turning to the scorpion in the משנה, רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that all harmful creatures may be killed on שבת. רב יוסף challenges this from a ברייתא listing only five. He then answers that רבי יהושע בן לוי means creatures chasing a person, where everyone agrees killing is permitted. The גמרא adds teachings and stories about killing snakes and scorpions, including a debate over whether pious behavior means refraining. It also asks whether רבי approved when a snake was killed in the בית המדרש, and it brings the rule that one may step on spit, a snake, or a scorpion לפי תומו. The amud ends with רבי חנינא's ruling that the candlesticks of רבי's house may be moved on שבת, and רבי זירא's question about which size he meant.

steps.title: The story: רב חנן is overlooked and hears אבין's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The hosts brought beds for the other guests but not for רב חנן בר רבא. He then found רבי אבין teaching his son a line about covering a child's feces.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought beds for the guests, but did not bring one for רב חנן בר רבא. He found אבין teaching his son: 'And one may place a bowl over a child's feces, because of the child.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that sets up the next move. רב חנן hears אבין teaching a version of our משנה that he is about to criticize.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The version being taught says the bowl covers a child's feces, so that the child does not touch them. Being left without a bed explains why רב חנן was irritated. The real issue is the wording of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: because of the child (so he won't touch it)

phrases.english: They brought beds for them,

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא לָא אַיְיתוֹ לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: but for Rav Chanan bar Rava they did not bring one.
He found him teaching his son:

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל צוֹאָה שֶׁל קָטָן מִפְּנֵי קָטָן.
phrases.english: "And over a child's feces, because of a child."
phrases.notes: Meaning: one may cover them with a bowl on שבת.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Version taught: one may cover a child's feces with a bowl on שבת to protect a child.

steps.title: רב חנן objects: the feces are fit for dogs
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן calls the teaching foolish. A child's feces are food for dogs, so they could simply be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: אבין the fool is teaching his son foolishness! Aren't the feces themselves prepared for dogs?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן attacks the wording that אבין taught. He argues that a child's feces are not מוקצה at all, so there is no need to cover them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anything that dogs can eat counts as usable, so it may be moved on שבת. If the feces may be moved, there is no point in teaching that one must cover them with a bowl.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Avin the fool is teaching folly to his son!
Aren't they themselves prepared for dogs?

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food for dogs is not מוקצה and may be moved, so covering it is unnecessary.

steps.title: Blocking a defense: rivers and springs are counted as prepared
steps.stepSummary: Someone might answer that these feces were not ready before שבת. רב חנן blocks that answer with a ברייתא about flowing water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the feces were not fit for use from yesterday — but it was taught: flowing rivers and gushing springs are like the feet of every person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן heads off a possible defense of אבין's wording. He brings a ברייתא as proof that his objection still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The possible defense is that the feces did not exist before שבת, so they were never prepared. The ברייתא answers this. Flowing water moves into a new area all the time, yet it is treated as if it were already there, because that is its normal nature. In the same way, a child relieves himself all the time, so his feces are treated as prepared from before שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you would say (blocks a possible answer)
but it was taught in a ברייתא
like the feet of every person (their תחום follows whoever draws the water)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not about feces at all. It is brought only to show that something that keeps arriving in a normal way counts as 'prepared' for שבת.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּלָא חַזְיָא לֵיהּ מֵאֶתְמוֹל —
phrases.english: And if you say it was not fit for it from yesterday —
but wasn't it taught:
flowing rivers and gushing springs —
they are like the feet of all people.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּלָא חַזְיָא לֵיהּ מֵאֶתְמוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the objection by closing off an escape route
steps.raayaObject: That a child's feces count as prepared for שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on rivers and springs being 'like the feet of every person'

steps.title: Avin asks how he should teach it
steps.stepSummary: אבין asks: if my wording is wrong, how should I teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then how should I teach it to him?
steps.whatsHappening: אבין accepts the criticism and asks for the correct wording. This sets up רב חנן's correction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question admits that a child's feces may be moved. What remains is to find a kind of feces that is truly unusable, so that covering it makes sense.

phrases.english: Rather, how should I teach it to him?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The correct wording of the משנה

steps.title: Corrected wording: chicken feces
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן says to teach it as chicken feces, covered for the sake of a child.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: over chicken feces, because of a child.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן gives the corrected text of the משנה. The feces are chicken feces, and the bowl protects the child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Chicken feces are not food for dogs, so they really are מוקצה. Because they cannot be moved, covering them with a bowl is the only option.

phrases.english: Say:

phrases.aramaic: עַל צוֹאָה שֶׁל תַּרְנְגוֹלִים מִפְּנֵי קָטָן.
phrases.english: over chicken feces, because of a child.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה refers to chicken feces, which are truly unusable.

steps.title: Why not remove it as a disgusting pot of waste?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: chicken feces should still be removable, because they count as a גרף של רעי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But derive that it may be removed because it is like a chamber pot of waste!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the corrected wording. Even chicken feces should be removable under the rule of גרף של רעי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something disgusting, like a chamber pot, may be carried out on שבת even though it is מוקצה. If chicken feces fall under that rule, they too could be removed rather than covered.

keyTerms.meaning: and let him derive it (from a simpler reason)
a chamber pot of waste (disgusting; may be removed on שבת)

phrases.english: But let him derive it
because it is like a chamber pot of waste!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּהָוֵי גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Disgusting matter may be removed as a גרף של רעי, so covering it should be unnecessary.

steps.title: רב אשי's mouse shows filth may be moved without a vessel
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say the rule applies only to waste inside a vessel. That is disproved by רב אשי, who had a mouse carried out by its tail.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say a chamber pot is allowed only because of its vessel, but the waste itself is not — what about the mouse found in רב אשי's spices? He told them: take it by its tail and remove it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible defense and strengthens its challenge with a story about רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The possible defense is that only a pot that holds waste may be moved, not loose waste. The story disproves that. רב אשי allowed a dead mouse to be removed directly, with no vessel. So disgusting matter may be moved by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: by means of / together with a vessel

phrases.english: And if you say:

phrases.aramaic: גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי אַגַּב מָנָא — אִין,
phrases.english: a chamber pot of waste, together with the vessel — yes,
but the waste itself — no,
but what about that mouse
that was found among Rav Ashi's spices,
and he said to them:
Take it by its tail and carry it out!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי אַגַּב מָנָא
steps.raayaObject: That disgusting matter may be removed even without a vessel
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב אשי and the mouse

steps.title: Answer: the feces were in a garbage heap
steps.stepSummary: The feces were in a garbage heap. There they do not bother anyone, so the גרף של רעי permission does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was in a garbage heap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by placing the case in a garbage heap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission to remove disgusting matter exists only where people live and are bothered by it. Feces in a garbage heap fit their surroundings, so removing them is not allowed. Only covering them is allowed.

phrases.english: In a garbage heap.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The feces were somewhere people live, where they could be removed
steps.terutzMaskana: They are in a garbage heap, where the removal permission does not apply

steps.title: What would a child be doing in a garbage heap?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this answer. A public garbage heap is not a place where a child would be.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is a child doing in a garbage heap?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the bowl is 'because of a child.' That makes no sense if the feces are in a garbage heap far from the house, where children are not found.

phrases.english: And what is a child doing in a garbage heap?

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A child would not be in a public garbage heap, so the reason 'because of a child' does not fit.

steps.title: Answer: in a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the feces were in a courtyard, where a child does play.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves the case to a courtyard to explain why a child is there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A courtyard is next to the home, and children play there. This solves the 'why is a child there' problem.

phrases.english: In a courtyard.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case is in a public garbage heap
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is in a courtyard

steps.title: But in a courtyard it would be removable
steps.stepSummary: In a courtyard, the feces would again count as a גרף של רעי and could be removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a courtyard too, it is a chamber pot of waste!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the courtyard answer brings back the original problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A courtyard is a place where people live. Filth there bothers people, so the גרף של רעי permission to remove it applies, and covering would be unnecessary.

phrases.aramaic: חָצֵר נָמֵי, גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי הוּא!
phrases.english: In a courtyard too, it is a chamber pot of waste!

steps.triggerLanguage: חָצֵר נָמֵי, גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי הוּא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Courtyard filth may be removed as a גרף של רעי, so the original challenge returns.

steps.title: Final answer: a garbage heap inside a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The case is a garbage heap located inside a courtyard. A child can reach it, but the feces do not count as a גרף של רעי there.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a garbage heap that is in a courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא combines both ideas into its final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the heap is in the courtyard, a child can wander over to it. Because it is a garbage heap, filth there is not out of place, so it may not be removed. That leaves covering with a bowl as the only option.

keyTerms.meaning: a garbage heap within a courtyard

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is about chicken feces (which are מוקצה) on a garbage heap inside a courtyard. It may not be removed as a גרף של רעי, but it may be covered to protect a child.

phrases.english: In a garbage heap that is in a courtyard.

steps.terutzMaskana: A garbage heap inside a courtyard: a child is present, but removal is not allowed

steps.title: The scorpion, and רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about covering a scorpion. רבי יהושע בן לוי then rules that all harmful creatures may be killed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And over a scorpion so that it won't bite.' רבי יהושע בן לוי said: All harmful creatures may be killed on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, the scorpion. It brings a broad rule from רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says to cover the scorpion. רבי יהושע בן לוי goes further and allows killing any harmful creature on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the focus of the challenge that follows (steps 14-16) and of רב יוסף's resolution in step 18.

phrases.english: "And over a scorpion, so that it will not bite."
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
All harmful creatures may be killed on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל הַמַּזִּיקִין נֶהֱרָגִין בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All harmful creatures may be killed on שבת.

steps.title: רב יוסף's challenge: a list of only five creatures
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges the rule with a ברייתא that lists only five creatures that may be killed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף challenged: Five may be killed on שבת: the fly of Egypt, the hornet of Nineveh, the scorpion of Chadyab, the snake of ארץ ישראל, and a mad dog anywhere.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף raises a challenge from a ברייתא that seems to limit the permission to five specific creatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names five deadly creatures, each in a place where it is especially dangerous. A specific list suggests the permission is limited, which clashes with 'all harmful creatures.'

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection:
Five may be killed on Shabbat, and these are they:
the fly that is in the land of Egypt,
and the hornet that is in Nineveh,
and the scorpion that is in Chadyab,
and the snake that is in Eretz Yisrael,
and a mad dog in any place.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that all harmful creatures may be killed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A list limited to five implies that the others may not be killed.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא? Not רבי יהודה's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the ברייתא follows. It cannot be רבי יהודה, who would forbid killing even these five.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say רבי יהודה — he said one is liable for a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out which תנא the ברייתא follows, to sharpen רב יוסף's challenge. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Killing a dangerous creature is done to get rid of it, not because the killer wants it dead for its own use. That is a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. רבי יהודה holds one is liable for such a מלאכה, so he would not allow killing even these five.

keyTerms.meaning: a forbidden act done not for its own intended purpose

phrases.english: Whose view is it?
If you say Rabbi Yehuda —

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמַר: מְלָאכָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה לְגוּפָהּ חַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ.
phrases.english: but he said: for a labor not needed for its own sake, one is liable.

steps.title: So it follows רבי שמעון, and only these five are allowed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must follow רבי שמעון. Even by his view only these five are allowed, which contradicts רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it רבי שמעון? And only these are permitted; others — not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes רב יוסף's challenge. Even under רבי שמעון's lenient approach, the ברייתא allows killing only five creatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds one is not liable for a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. Even so, the ברייתא limits the permission to five deadly creatures. That implies other harmful creatures may not be killed, against רבי יהושע בן לוי. רבי ירמיה first questions the ברייתא (step 17), and רב יוסף gives the real answer in step 18.
steps.confusionAlert: Even רבי שמעון does not allow every harmful creature here. The ברייתא's five are only the deadly ones, and that is exactly why it is a challenge to רבי יהושע בן לוי.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not Rabbi Shimon?
And only these are permitted; others — no!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that all harmful creatures may be killed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי שמעון the ברייתא permits only five creatures, implying other harmful creatures may not be killed.

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא is not reliable
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה pushes back on רב יוסף's challenge. He asks how we know the ברייתא listing five creatures is an accurate text. Perhaps it is corrupted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Who says this ברייתא is accurate? Maybe it is a corrupted text.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה tries to defend רבי יהושע בן לוי. He questions whether the ברייתא used against him is even a reliable text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's challenge depended completely on the ברייתא that lists only five creatures. If that ברייתא is corrupted, the challenge falls apart. רבי ירמיה is not answering the contradiction itself. He is attacking the source it rests on.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
And who will tell us
that this (baraita) is accurate?
Perhaps it is corrupted?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן נֵימָא לַן דְּהָא מְתָרַצְתָּא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי יהושע בן לוי against the contradiction raised in Steps 14-16 by questioning the ברייתא's reliability.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the challenge from the ברייתא by questioning whether the text can be relied on at all.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge rests on a text that may be corrupted.

steps.title: When the creatures are chasing him, everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the ברייתא is reliable, since he himself taught it. He answers his own challenge: רבי יהושע בן לוי was speaking about creatures that are chasing a person, and in that case everyone permits killing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I taught this ברייתא, I raised the challenge from it, and I will answer it. רבי יהושע בן לוי is speaking about creatures running after a person, and then everyone agrees it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף stands by the ברייתא and gives the real answer. רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling is about a case of real, immediate danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא with five creatures is about killing them in general, when they are not attacking. רבי יהושע בן לוי is talking about a creature actively chasing someone. That is real danger to life, so even רבי יהודה would permit killing it. The contradiction is gone because the two sources describe different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: When they are running after him

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן לוי's permission to kill any harmful creature applies when it is chasing a person. Real danger makes it permitted according to all opinions.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
I taught it (the baraita),
and I raised the objection from it,
and I will answer it:
When they are running after him, and it is the opinion of all.
phrases.notes: Refers to רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא מַתְנֵינָא לַהּ וְאוֹתֵיבְנָא לַהּ וַאֲנָא מְתָרֵיצְנָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי ירמיה's doubt about the text and resolves the original contradiction in a different way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation: the two sources refer to different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע בן לוי allowed killing any harmful creature in any situation, which contradicts the ברייתא's list of five.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהושע בן לוי speaks of creatures actively chasing a person. In that case killing is permitted by everyone.

steps.title: Pious people are displeased with killing snakes on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רבא בר רב הונא. The pious are not pleased with someone who kills snakes and scorpions on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רבא בר רב הונא: If someone kills snakes and scorpions on שבת, the pious are not pleased with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about killing snakes and scorpions on שבת. It sets up a response from רבא בר רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Killing these creatures may be technically allowed, but the ברייתא says pious people disapprove. It is a statement about a higher standard of piety, not about what the strict law forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: A reciter of ברייתות in the study hall
Pious people who go beyond the letter of the law
They are not pleased with him

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rava bar Rav Huna:
One who kills snakes and scorpions on Shabbat —
the spirit of the pious is not pleased with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related topic: the attitude toward killing harmful creatures on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pious disapprove of killing snakes and scorpions on שבת.

steps.title: The חכמים are displeased with those pious people
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב הונא answers that the חכמים are not pleased with those pious people. Snakes and scorpions are dangerous, so holding back from killing them is not proper piety.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And with those pious people, the חכמים are not pleased.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב הונא rejects the attitude of the pious described in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He turns the ברייתא's own phrase back on it. The חכמים are displeased with the pious, because refusing to kill dangerous creatures puts people at risk. Being "extra careful" about שבת is wrong when lives are involved.

phrases.english: He said to him:
And those pious people —
the spirit of the Sages is not pleased with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹתָן חֲסִידִים אֵין רוּחַ חֲכָמִים נוֹחָה מֵהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the ברייתא of Step 19 and rejects its approach.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the value judgment of the pious, not the existence of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Refraining from killing dangerous creatures endangers people, so it is not true piety.

steps.title: רב הונא disapproves of killing a hornet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבא בר רב הונא's view disagrees with his father רב הונא. רב הונא saw a man killing a hornet and sarcastically asked whether he had finished killing all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רב הונא. רב הונא saw a man killing a hornet and said to him: Have you finished off all of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב הונא held differently from his son. It proves this with a short story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's sarcastic question means that killing one hornet does not remove the danger, since there are many more. So he saw no reason to kill it, which matches the attitude of the pious. This puts him against his son רבא בר רב הונא.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rav Huna.
For Rav Huna saw a certain man
who was killing a hornet,
he said to him: Have you finished off all of them?
phrases.notes: Sarcastic: killing one does nothing, so why do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notes that רבא בר רב הונא's view in Step 20 conflicts with רב הונא's behavior.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא disapproved of needlessly killing a single harmful creature, siding with the attitude of the pious.

steps.title: What it means when snakes cross your path
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if snakes and scorpions came before a person and he killed them, they were sent so that he would kill them. If he did not kill them, they were sent to kill him, and a miracle saved him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: If snakes and scorpions came upon someone and he killed them, it is clear they came so he would kill them. If he did not kill them, it is clear they came to kill him, and a miracle from heaven saved him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the meaning behind meeting dangerous creatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the meeting as directed from heaven. If the person killed the creatures, that was their purpose. If he did not, and he survived, he was saved by a miracle.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If snakes and scorpions happened upon him,
if he killed them — it is known that they came to him so he would kill them.
If he did not kill them — it is known that they came to kill him
and a miracle from heaven was done for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן נִזְדַּמְּנוּ לוֹ נְחָשִׁים וְעַקְרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of meeting and killing harmful creatures, adding a heavenly perspective.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meeting snakes and scorpions is directed from heaven. Killing them fulfills that purpose, and surviving without killing them is a miracle.

steps.title: Only when they were touching him
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the ברייתא. It speaks about creatures that actually brushed against the person. Only then is surviving clearly a miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא, and some say רבה בר בר חנה, said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is when they were brushing against him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains which case the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing a snake from far away does not mean it came to kill you. The ברייתא's conclusion fits only when the creatures were touching the person and still did him no harm. In that case, being saved really was a miracle.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another name for the speaker)
When they were brushing against / touching him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר עוּלָּא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: Ulla said, and some say it was Rabba bar bar Ḥana,
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
This is when they were brushing against him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the case of the ברייתא in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא applies when the creatures were actually touching the person.

steps.title: A snake in the בית המדרש killed by a נבטי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא tells of a snake that fell into the בית המדרש. A נבטי (non-Jew) killed it. רבי said: one of its kind met it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר כהנא said: Once a snake fell into the בית המדרש, and a נבטי got up and killed it. רבי said: Its match met it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a snake that was killed in the בית המדרש. This sets up the next step, which asks what רבי meant by his remark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's sharp remark, 'one of its kind met it,' compares the נבטי who killed the snake to the snake itself. Whether רבי meant this as approval of the killing or as disapproval is exactly what the next step asks.
steps.confusionAlert: The word "אֶחָד" (one) in "נָפַל אֶחָד" refers to a snake, even though the text does not say so. The text holds back from naming it outright.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said:

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת נָפַל אֶחָד בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ,
phrases.english: Once, one (a snake) fell into the study hall,
and a certain Nabatean stood up and killed it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי: פָּגַע בּוֹ כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ!
phrases.english: Rabbi said: One of its kind met it!

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּעַם אַחַת נָפַל אֶחָד בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of killing harmful creatures with a story whose meaning is debated in the next step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a snake fell into the בית המדרש, a non-Jew killed it, and רבי remarked that a harmful one met its match.

steps.title: Did רבי approve of killing the snake?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי meant by 'one of its kind met it': was the killing proper or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: when רבי said 'one of its kind met it,' did he mean the man acted properly, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the snake story from the last step. It asks how to understand רבי's comment about the נבטי who killed the snake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'פגע בו כיוצא בו' (one of its kind met it) can be read two ways. It may praise the act: the snake met its proper end. Or it may be a put-down: only a non-Jew, a 'creature like it,' would kill on שבת, and a Jew should not. The גמרא wants to know which reading is right.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars (an open question)
One of its kind met it

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:
"One of its kind met it"
phrases.notes: Quoting רבי's comment from the previous step.

phrases.english: does it mean that he acted properly, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to read רבי's remark in the story told in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי's words approve of killing a snake on שבת or disapprove of it.

steps.title: רבי ינאי would kill even a hornet on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A story about רבי ינאי is brought to show that killing snakes and scorpions on שבת is proper.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אבא son of רבי חייא בר אבא and רבי זירא were sitting in the courtyard of רבי ינאי's house. A question came up between them, and they asked רבי ינאי: May one kill snakes and scorpions on שבת? He told them: I would kill a hornet. A snake and a scorpion — all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from a story. רבי ינאי says he would kill a hornet on שבת, so of course he would kill a snake or a scorpion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a קל וחומר: a hornet is less dangerous than a snake or scorpion. If a hornet may be killed, a snake surely may be. So killing the snake in the בית המדרש was proper, and רבי's words should be read as approval.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof is coming)
All the more so (a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: Come and hear,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: that Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Chiya bar Abba,
and Rabbi Zeira were sitting
in the courtyard of Rabbi Yannai's house.
A question came up between them,
and they asked Rabbi Yannai:
What is the law about killing snakes and scorpions on Shabbat?
He said to them: I would kill a hornet,
a snake and a scorpion — all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question of step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That killing a snake on שבת is proper, so רבי approved.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ינאי's קל וחומר from a hornet to a snake and scorpion.

steps.title: Maybe only by stepping on it casually
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: perhaps רבי ינאי allowed it only by stepping on the creature as if by chance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he meant only by stepping on it in a casual way, as if by chance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. Maybe רבי ינאי did not allow killing on purpose, only crushing it underfoot while walking normally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לפי תומו' means acting innocently, as if you did not plan it. If רבי ינאי meant only this casual way, his words do not prove that the open killing by the נבטי was proper. So the question from step 25 is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: Innocently, casually, as if by chance

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say killing a snake is forbidden. It only says רבי ינאי's words may refer to a narrower, casual way of doing it, so they cannot prove the bigger point.

phrases.english: Perhaps only innocently (stepping on it as if by chance).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from רבי ינאי in step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide the question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי ינאי's permission may be limited to stepping on it casually, not killing it openly.

steps.title: Sources for stepping on things casually
steps.stepSummary: Statements of רב יהודה, רב ששת and רב קטינא show that stepping on spit, a snake, or a scorpion לפי תומו is a known idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said: Spit — one may step on it casually. And רב ששת said: A snake — one may step on it casually. And רב קטינא said: A scorpion — one may step on it casually.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its rejection. It shows that אמוראים really did speak about stepping on things casually on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spitting on the ground and rubbing it in could look like smoothing the floor, which is a שבת concern, but casual stepping is allowed. רב ששת and רב קטינא use the same wording for a snake and a scorpion. This shows the limited reading of רבי ינאי is realistic.

keyTerms.meaning: He steps on it, tramples it

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said:
Spit — one may step on it innocently.
And Rav Sheshet said:
A snake — one may step on it innocently.
And Rav Ketina said:
A scorpion — one may step on it innocently.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in step 27 with real sources.
steps.raayaObject: That 'לפי תומו' is a real rule, so the limited reading of רבי ינאי makes sense.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rules of רב יהודה (spit), רב ששת (snake), and רב קטינא (scorpion).
steps.whatToRemember: The question from step 25 stays open. רבי ינאי's words may only allow stepping on a snake or scorpion casually, not killing it openly.

steps.title: אבא בר מניומי and the spit at the ריש גלותא's house
steps.stepSummary: A debtor quotes רב יהודה's rule about spit, and the ריש גלותא sees he is a תלמיד חכם and lets him go.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא בר מרתא, who is also called אבא בר מניומי, owed money to the people of the ריש גלותא's house. They brought him and were pressuring him. There was spit on the floor. The ריש גלותא said to his people: Bring a vessel and turn it over on top of it. אבא said to them: You do not need to. This is what רב יהודה said: Spit — one may step on it casually. The ריש גלותא said to them: He is a young תלמיד חכם. Let him go.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that uses רב יהודה's rule about spit from the step before. Quoting the rule shows the ריש גלותא that the debtor is a Torah scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ריש גלותא wanted to cover the spit so no one would step on it on שבת. אבא בר מניומי knew the rule that stepping on it casually is fine, so no cover was needed. His knowledge made him respected, and he was released.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, leader of the Jews in Bavel
Turn it upside down over it
Leave him alone, let him go

phrases.english: Abba bar Marta,
who is Abba bar Manyomi,

phrases.aramaic: הֲווֹ מַסְּקִי בֵּיהּ דְּבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא זוּזֵי.
phrases.english: owed money to the people of the Exilarch's house.
They brought him and were pressuring him.
There was spit lying there.
The Exilarch said to them:
Bring a vessel and turn it over on top of it.
He said to them: You do not need to,
this is what Rabbi Yehuda said:
Spit — one may step on it innocently.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן הוּא, שִׁבְקוּהּ.
phrases.english: He said to them: He is a young Torah scholar, let him go.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא בַּר מָרְתָא דְּהוּא אַבָּא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that applies רב יהודה's rule about spit from step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no need to cover spit on שבת; stepping on it casually is allowed.

steps.title: The candlesticks of רבי's house may be moved on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא quotes רבי חנינא: the candlesticks of רבי's house may be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר כהנא said in the name of רבי חנינא: The candlesticks of רבי's house may be moved on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. Since it just quoted רבי אבא בר כהנא (step 24), it brings another ruling he reported, about moving candlesticks on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a candlestick is used for a forbidden act on שבת (lighting), so one might think it is מוקצה. רבי חנינא says the candlesticks of רבי's house may be moved. This sets up the next question about which kind of candlestick he meant.

keyTerms.meaning: The house of רבי יהודה הנשיא

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said
that Rabbi Chanina said:
The candlesticks of the house of Rabbi
may be moved on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, linked only because the same speaker (רבי אבא בר כהנא) was quoted earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The candlesticks of רבי's house may be moved on שבת.

steps.title: Small candlesticks or large ones?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks whether this means candlesticks moved with one hand or also with two hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: Does this mean candlesticks that are moved with one hand, or even ones that are moved with two hands?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks a question to define the ruling. He wants to know which size of candlestick is meant, which sets up the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A candlestick lifted with one hand is small and light. One that needs two hands is big and heavy, and people usually do not move it. רבי זירא asks whether the permission covers only the small ones or the big ones too.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to him:
Does this mean ones moved with one hand,
or even ones moved with two hands?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the ruling of step 30 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the permission covers only one-hand candlesticks or also heavy two-hand ones.
